I am 54 years old and have worked this land in Quzhou County for 30 years. With 11 people under my roof and some of the younger generation working off-farm in town, I need to balance food security for the household with cash income, while not taking on more labor than my family can manage. My farm is 10.9 mu, and I have a reliable well for irrigation.

This year, I will keep my trusted wheat-maize double cropping system on 8 mu of my best land. Wheat and maize are the backbone of my household — we eat the wheat and feed the maize to our animals. The remaining 2.9 mu I will plant with cotton. Cotton brings good money, but it is labor-intensive, especially the pest spraying. With some family members working outside, 2.9 mu is all I can handle.

For **winter wheat**, I will use an improved variety and rotary tillage before sowing in October. I sow about 35 jin of seed per mu. I apply compound fertilizer as a basal dressing and topdress with urea at green-up time in spring. I will irrigate three times through the season — my well water is precious but necessary for a good wheat crop. I expect around 900 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For **summer maize**, I plant right after the wheat harvest in early June. I use Denghai 605 hybrid seed — it yields well and resists lodging. I sow directly without tillage to save time and fuel. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat, and I irrigate twice during the summer. I expect about 1,000 kg per mu.

For **cotton**, I till in spring with the rotary tiller and sow an improved variety at about 3 jin per mu. Cotton needs plenty of fertilizer and I apply a compound dressing. I irrigate twice, but the real work is pest control — I will spray insecticides and herbicides about 14 times through the season to protect the bolls. I expect around 500 kg of seed cotton per mu.
